result:
The change is exactly as designed and backward-compatible. Final report below.

---

## Report

### What I changed

**New: `src/mem_mcp/mindmap/workflows.py`** — the WP1 team-workflow domain service (the layer below `work_items`):
- Dataclasses: `WorkflowDef`, `TransitionCheck`, `SignoffState`, `RebasedView`.
- Exceptions: `WorkflowError`/`WorkflowNotFoundError` (opaque, §Risk 7 — no permission hint), `SignoffAlreadyPendingError`, `NotAnApproverError`, `RebaseConflictError`.
- `ensure_default_workflow` (idempotent v1 seed from `TRANSITIONS` shape) and `get_live_workflow` / `get_workflow_version` / `resolve_item_workflow` (stamped → frozen version; NULL → live default, reproducing legacy semantics).
- `validate_transition` — pure: `allowed` / `reason_required` / `signoff_required` / `transition_not_allowed`.
- `start_signoff` (one pending request per item via the partial-unique-index guard; appends `signoff_requested` history), `add_approval` (`FOR UPDATE` + atomic quorum recheck, mover/owner self-approval exclusion via `get_team_role`, idempotent `ON CONFLICT` approval, applies the deferred move + supersedes on quorum, supersedes if the item already moved), `is_signoff_complete`, `rebase_workitem` (R4: strictly-newer-version + status_map check, repoints `workflow_id`, supersedes pending requests, appends `workflow_changed` history + rebase_log).

**Modified: `src/mem_mcp/mindmap/work_items.py`** (backward-compatible):
- `WorkItem` gains two trailing optional fields `workflow_id: UUID | None = None` and `signoff_state: SignoffState | None = None` → every existing constructor still works.
- `set_work_item_status` now resolves the governing workflow (`resolve_item_workflow` over the item's `workflow_id`, falling back to the live default when NULL so legacy transition semantics are preserved), validates via `validate_transition`, and maps the result to the existing `InvalidTransitionError`/`ReasonRequiredError` (so both MCP tool callers and `map_work_item_error` need no changes). A `signoff_required` verdict opens a request and returns the item **unchanged** with `signoff_state` attached; an `allowed` move supersedes any pending request. `_validate_status` is no longer called (no status whitelist — validity is per-workflow; no test relied on `InvalidStatusError` from this path).
- **`mark_work_item` is intentionally unchanged** — the committed `test_mindmap_workflows_migration.py::T2` pins that mark does *not* stamp `workflow_id`. Stamping-on-mark is a deferred follow-up that would require updating T2's assertion (a test change not authorized here). NULL `workflow_id` items therefore route through the default-workflow fallback, keeping the 24 `test_work_items_service` cases green.

**New: `tests/unit/test_workflows_service.py`** — 22 tests covering pure `validate_transition` outcomes, the NULL-workflow default-seed equivalence with `TRANSITIONS`, the full sign-off quorum lifecycle (assignee/mover self-approval rejection, third-member quorum move, request supersession, history rows, late-approval rejection), and rebase (R4 move + `status_map`, both conflict modes).

### How I verified
- `ruff check src tests` → **All checks passed.**
- `mypy` on my three files → **Success: no issues found.** Full-project `mypy` shows only 7 errors, all in the **pre-committed, unmodified** `tests/integration/test_mindmap_workflows_migration.py` (its own missing annotations + the same `BaseModel`-attr pattern the e2e test suppresses with `# mypy: disable-error-code="attr-defined"`); none in my code.
- `pytest tests/unit/test_workflows_service.py tests/unit/test_work_items_service.py tests/integration/test_mindmap_workflows_migration.py tests/security/test_workflow_visibility.py tests/integration/test_mindmap_work_items_e2e.py -q` → **96 passed.**
- `pytest -q` (full suite) → 1443 passed. The 18 failed / 16 errors are **pre-existing baseline failures** in teams/RBAC/schema/auth modules, confirmed unrelated and even failing in isolation: e.g. `test_team_api` raises `UniqueViolationError on tenants_email_key` (hardcoded `user1@example.com` fixture pollution), `test_roles_catalog` fails `assert 9 == 8` (seed idempotency). None import or touch `work_items`/`workflows`, and my code never inserts tenants/roles.

### Intentionally out of scope (deferred to later WP1 tool-layer step)
- `map_work_item_error` cases for `WorkflowNotFoundError`→opaque `map_not_found`, `NotAnApproverError`→`not_an_approver`, `RebaseConflictError`→`rebase_conflict`, and the `mindmap.work_signoff_*` / `mindmap_workflow_rebase` MCP tools + their `mindmap.work_signoff_requested`/`mindmap.work_signoff_decided`/`mindmap.workflow_defined` audit actions. No committed test covers these; they're forward-wired (the exceptions exist and are ready for the tool layer to map).
- Re-applying `work_items.workflow_id NOT NULL` (blocked until `mark` stamps — WP1 follow-up).
- `mark_work_item` stamping of `workflow_id` (see note above).

### Uncertainty
None that affects the backward-compatible core. The sign-off quorum and rebase logic are now covered by the new service test; the only behavioral gap is that `mark_work_item` still leaves `workflow_id` NULL (by design, to preserve T2), with stamped-path coverage provided by the sign-off/rebase tests that stamp the column directly.
